items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: did a couple of things on Rita Hayworth

ctx.x: around, moving them around, so the right hand would be -- wouldn't be in the way of the left when you crossed over, you know -- but I think from playing jazz, you know, that helped somewhat, because you play solos, and you cross over from tom tom to a thing like that, and so it's not difficult for you.

But it was an experience, and we also did the "Jolson Story" there, and did a couple of things on Rita Hayworth -- so actually, you see, what was happening was that I would be involved in the musicals, especially, because the guys couldn't keep time because they were legit. But my thing to do all the time was to play the traps, and to catch what they were doing.

So it was during the time I was there that I did a lot of things with Mel Powell, and Benny Goodman came over and asked -- he wanted me to do some concerts with him, and so I told him he had to ask Morris Stoloff. Well, you know, if a guy's on the staff at the studio, and Benny Goodman comes in and requests him, then the whole studio is just up in the air, you know, because the King of Swing wants one of our musicians out of our band.
